evidence: Both clubs' supporters sing You'll Never Walk Alone as their anthem; at the 2016 Europa League tie on the Hillsborough anniversary the two crowds sang it together, which won both sets of fans the FIFA Fan Award.
Feyenoord adopted You'll Never Walk Alone (Lee Towers' 1976 version) as a club anthem; Feyenoord's travelling fans sang it in tribute to Arne Slot when he moved to Liverpool.
Mainz 05 sing You'll Never Walk Alone before home matches (one of only two German clubs, with Dortmund); the link is often highlighted through Jurgen Klopp, who managed both clubs.
Club Brugge are listed among clubs whose supporters adopted You'll Never Walk Alone; no documented mutual recognition with Liverpool found.
Genoa are listed among clubs whose supporters adopted You'll Never Walk Alone; no documented mutual recognition with Liverpool found.

A long-standing fan friendship dating from the 1973, 1977 and 1978 European meetings, strengthened when Gladbach fans raised money for Hillsborough families; supporters still visit each other's grounds.
Friendly relations between the fans grew after the 1965 European Cup quarter-final decided by a coin toss; German Wikipedia says only a few friendship scarves remain of it.
Lazio's ultras count West Ham among their main international friendships, which grew from fan contacts and the shared love of Paolo Di Canio; supporters attend each other's matches.
Lazio fans previously had a strong twinning with Chelsea supporters, which cooled as the West Ham tie grew; still listed on some twinning maps.

Sections of both fan bases share a friendship that began when Wearside shipbuilders worked in Rotterdam in the 1970s and 80s; a 'Feyenoord Mackems' branch travels to the Stadium of Light with its own flag.
After the 1985 League Cup final, where Sunderland fans applauded Norwich's lap of honour and the fans swapped scarves, the clubs have played for a 'Friendship Trophy' whenever they meet.
After Sunderland's 2005 pre-season visit to Portland, a group of 31 Timbers Army members travelled to watch Sunderland at Seaham; no evidence of an ongoing formal tie.
Cordial relations between the fans date from 1997, when Doncaster were the last visitors to the Goldstone Ground during Brighton's ownership crisis and both players and fans supported Brighton.
Juventus took their black-and-white stripes from Notts County shirts shipped to Turin in the early 1900s; Juventus invited Notts County to play the opening match of the Juventus Stadium in 2011.
In 1886 Forest donated a set of red kits to help the newly formed Arsenal establish themselves; Arsenal still wear red.
In 1909 Athletic's Juan Elorduy bought 50 Southampton shirts in Southampton, and Athletic have worn red-and-white stripes since January 1910; the clubs have marked the link with friendlies.
Half of the Southampton shirts Elorduy bought in 1909 went to Athletic's Madrid branch, the future Atlético Madrid, who adopted red-and-white stripes in 1911.
The professional Crystal Palace club was formed in 1905 under Aston Villa assistant secretary Edmund Goodman and wore Villa's claret and blue until 1973.
